channel.title: RGUHS MD Pharmacology — Practicals, Narrated
channel.itunes:author: Dr. Harshad Ramineni
channel.description: Narrated model answers for the RGUHS MD Pharmacology practical examination, kept apart from the theory-exam show. Season 1, protocol writing: eight model protocols, from a phase 2 anxiolytic trial to phase 3 registration programmes, each with its design, sample size, visit schedule, analysis, Indian regulatory and ethics requirements, and viva points. Season 2, experimental pharmacology: laboratory animals and ethics, laboratory and sophisticated instruments, and the in vivo experiments of Medhi's Practical Manual, one episode per item, then nine animal workshop equipment monographs set against the textbooks. Season 3, bioassay: the principles, the designs and their calculations worked from the textbook's own numbers, the isolated tissues and every determine-the-unknown-concentration experiment, and the isolated heart. Season 4, chemical analysis and graphs: the tests for alkaloids, sterols and glycosides, how to identify an unknown sample, and every chart tracing, from adrenaline reversal to the frog rectus. Season 5, pharmacokinetic problems: the formula sheet and fourteen problems, each worked by hand from the given values to the answer, then nine PG-level problems from the clinical pharmacokinetics textbooks. Season 6, clinical cases: the eleven clinical cases, from stable angina to type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease, each with the diagnosis, the drug treatment with doses and monitoring, and the viva questions. Season 7, pedagogy viva: the questions examiners ask after the microteaching session, from OHP and DOAP to Bloom's taxonomy, item analysis and CBME, each with the answer to lead with. Season 8, microteaching theory: what microteaching is, its component skills and cycle, writing objectives, slide design, and the viva questions on the session, with how the six exam decks apply them. Season 9, grand viva: rapid viva questions on the basics, general pharmacology and the autonomic nervous system, the drug groups of every system with their uses and hallmark adverse effects, then three on every question of the four September 2026 theory papers, each with the answer to say first. About 51 hours 26 minutes.
